title: Node Autopsy: Helm & Node Lifecycle Scratchpad
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad while debugging a weird node lifecycle issue in a dev cluster (gke-autoscale-ish). Symptoms: nodes go NotReady intermittently after image/taint changes, pods stuck Terminating or stuck in Pending with MountVolume.WaitForAttach timeout. Happens after helm upgrades that touch daemonset + node-labeling hook. Suspect race between kubelet, attach/detach controller, and a Helm post-install hook that mutates node labels/taints.

Timeline of attempts and observations:
- 2025-11-03 09:15: First noticed alert: node-gke-dev-5a NotReady for ~3m, then returned Ready. Alert noise repeated across 3 nodes in the same zone.
- 2025-11-03 09:20: Ran kubectl get nodes -o wide: saw NotReady briefly and kernel messages on node: low random? unrelated.
- 2025-11-03 09:28: Pattern: coincides with helm release "agent-daemon v3.1.4" being deployed (auto CI). That release includes new nodeAffinity change and post-install job that labels nodes with workload-type=agent.

Commands tried (with snippets):
- kubectl get nodes -w
  > node-gke-dev-5a   NotReady  2d   10.32.3.14  gke-us-west1-a   1.25.7-gke.1200

- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,120p'
  > Nov 03 09:15:31 node kernel: audit: type=1400 apparmor=DENIED
  > Nov 03 09:16:02 kubelet[2090]: E1103 09:16:02.123456   2090 kubelet_node_status.go:202] Error updating node status: Operation cannot be fulfilled, object was modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again

- kubectl describe pod agent-daemon-abcde -n infra
  > Events:
  >   Warning  FailedMount  3s (x18 over 2m)  kubelet  MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "data-pv" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = attach timeout

- kubectl get csiprovisioner logs: attach/detach controller shows detach then attach loops for same volume id.

Hypotheses:
1) Helm post-install job labels nodes while kubelet is mid-restart (e.g., kubelet restarted by systemd for config change) -> node object update conflict causes transient NotReady and controller churn.
2) Volume attach/detach timeouts are because node identity changed (labels/taints) and cloud-provider detaches/reattaches as part of migration.
3) Daemonset update strategy is "RollingUpdate" with maxUnavailable: 1 -> when a node is cordoned/tainted by the job, kube-svc controllers move pods -> volume detach order races with delete/termination grace causing stale attach records in cloud provider.

Notes-to-self (commands I used to reproduce-ish):
- Force helm upgrade locally with --wait --timeout 10m and watch nodes: helm upgrade infra-agent ./chart -n infra --wait --timeout 10m
- Simulate labeling job: kubectl label nodes node-gke-dev-5a workload-type=agent --overwrite
- Observe attach/detach controller: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/kube-controller-manager | grep "attach" -n
- Check cloud provider detach: gcloud compute instances detach-disk --zone us-west1-a --disk=projects/… (didn't run in prod)

Useful debugging snippets I saved: (copy/paste friendly)
- kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status} {.metadata.resourceVersion}\n'
- kubectl patch node node-gke-dev-5a -p '{"metadata":{"labels":{"workload-type":"agent-debug"}}}' --type=merge
- kubectl cordon node-gke-dev-5a && kubectl drain node-gke-dev-5a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Observed errors and raw snippets:
- "Error updating node status: Operation cannot be fulfilled, object was modified" — suggests concurrent updates to node object (kubelet status vs server-side labeler).
- MountVolume.WaitForAttach timeout in kubelet: suggests cloud attach step failing or delayed.
- controller-manager logs: "volume detached, but still in use" occasionally echoed.

Experiment matrix (what I tried and outcome):
- Case A: Disabled Helm post-install job (commented out) + apply labels manually after all nodes stable -> result: no immediate NotReady spikes, attach timeouts disappeared for 10m window. Implication: job timing matters.
- Case B: Change daemonset updateStrategy to maxUnavailable: 20% -> fewer nodes updated at once, still saw one NotReady but less frequent.
- Case C: Add pre-stop hook to agent daemonset to sleep 10s to give kubelet time to finish detach -> mixed results, increased graceful termination but didn't solve race entirely.

Root-cause theory (current):
A race between a Helm post-install labeling job (which mutates node metadata/taints) and kubelet status updates + cloud volume attach/detach leads to short windows where the kube-controller-manager tries to reassign pods while kubelet or cloud attach processes are mid-operation. The concurrent writes to node object trigger conflicts; attach/detach loops cause MountVolume timeouts.

Temporary mitigations I tested: (low-risk)
- Make Helm job idempotent and gated: add retry with exponential backoff and filter for nodes in Ready state before labeling (kubectl get nodes --field-selector status.conditions.type=Ready,status.conditions.status=True)
- Turn Helm job into a CronJob that runs 1m after upgrade (gives rolling updates time to settle).
- Set daemonset updateStrategy to surge/percentage tuned to cluster size (avoid too many detach ops simultaneously).
- Add RBAC to prevent non-control-plane agents from updating node.status — but this is sketchy; kubelet must update status. Instead restrict labelers to patch metadata only (not status).

Next steps (todo):
- [x] Reproduce in staging with helm release flow and --wait=false to simulate CI timing.
- [ ] Open a Linear ticket with timeline and attach controller logs (PLT-412 linked).
- [ ] Update Helm chart to only label nodes that are Ready (add selector + retry loop) and merge PR (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/986).
- [ ] Add a preflight job in CI to run "kubectl get nodes" and abort helm deploy if >10% NotReady.
- [ ] Consult GCP support if attach/detach timeouts persist after labeling change.

Questions to ask Priya/infra team:
- Is there a reason the labeling job needs to run as a post-install hook synchronously? Could it be deferred?
- Do we have any cloud-provider-level automation that triggers disk migration on label changes? (I doubt but need confirmation.)

Random personal notes:
- Keep a small delay (30s) before labeling for now in hotfix to reduce blast radius.
- Consider switching to node feature discovery or daemonset-based labeling instead of a global hook.

Links referenced during debugging: (keepsakes)
- kube-controller-manager attach/detach design: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/component-kube-controller-manager/
- GKE attach/detach doc snippets: https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/persistent-volumes

If this regresses again, capture kubelet /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/* and controller-manager logs with timestamps and attach to ticket. Also plan for an outage window if we need to change default updateStrategy cluster-wide.

-- Evan (notes to self, messy, will clean into PR description once hypothesis validated)
